banner.no_coding_agent: No coding agent is configured yet — without one, no runs can be started.
api.archive_only_finished: only finished runs can be archived
api.model_id_shape: model ID does not look like author/slug
overview.rename: Rename this run (the agent keeps its name)
overview.archive: Move to archive (report and log stay intact)

usage.title: Subscription usage
norepo.title: Create a repo first
norepo.text: Agents and runs always belong to exactly one repo. Example:
agents.name: Name
agents.flows_hint: Flows hang on an agent or a single run — attach them in the form below.
agents.delete_confirm: Delete agent "{name}"? Its runs stay untouched.
agents.move_hint: The agent moves to the selected repo. If the name is already taken there, a date-time suffix is appended.
agents.move_bad_repo: The target repo does not exist.
agents.move_same_repo: The agent already lives in that repo.
agents.name_taken: An agent named "{name}" already exists in this repo.
runform.title: Single run — repo "{repo}"
runform.title_ph: leave empty: generated from the prompt
runform.title_hint: Empty field: a cheap model at OpenRouter derives a short title from the prompt (Settings → Run titles). Every title can be renamed later in the overview.
goal.legend: Goal (optional) — when is this run done?
goal.ph: all tests in test/ pass and the branch is pushed
goal.hint: Typed into the session as "/goal <condition>" right after the start. Claude then checks after every turn whether the condition holds and keeps taking turns by itself until it does — or until it judges it impossible. Only Claude Code knows this; the field disappears for every other coding agent.
goal.title: Goal
goal.pending: not sent yet — waiting for the session
goal.never_sent: never sent: the run was over before the session took it
runform.pipeline_on_hint: Pipeline is on — scheduled starts run as well.
runform.pipeline_off_hint: Pipeline is off — that only gates the scheduled agent starts; this run is not held up by it.
start.mode_idle: as soon as no other run of this repo is going
start.idle_hint: The run waits in the overview and starts by itself as soon as the repo is free. Several waiting runs start one after another, not at once.
start.err_at: Start time is missing or unreadable.
start.err_in: The number of minutes must be greater than 0.
start.until_free: starts as soon as the repo is free
start.err_not_deferred: Only a deferred run can be started this way.
run.terminal_after: (the run is over — the coding agent is still sitting in its session)
run.session_after_hint: This run is finished and its report is written. Whatever you send here is new work in the same session — this run will not record it any more, and the session closes by itself once the keep time is up (Settings → tmux session).
run.end_session_hint: frees the memory of the process still sitting there; log, report and the record of this run stay
run.send_text_ph: Send text into the session (multi-line possible)
run.retry_hint: starts the same task again; an existing worktree is reused
run.archive_hint: An archived run is hidden from the overview but stays fully readable here.
run.harness_not_configured: Coding agent "{harness}" is not configured or disabled — add it under Settings → Coding agents.
run.edit.duration_hint: Sets the traffic-light thresholds and the overview's expectation from now on. The running agent is not told.
run.edit.prompt_hint: The run has not started yet — it will launch with this prompt.
run.edit.repo_hint: Moves the run to another repo; the planned start time stays.
run.edit.duration_only_planned: A run that is already over cannot be given a new expected duration.
run.edit.prompt_only_planned: Only a run that has not started yet can be given a new prompt.
run.edit.repo_only_planned: Only a run that has not started yet can be moved to another repo.
run.edit.duration_invalid: The expected duration must be at least 1 minute.
skills.title: Extra skills
skills.legend: Extra skills (opt-in, become an instruction in the prompt)
incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.needs_you_hint: Login, credits or model: this does not clear itself — every following run walks into the same wall. Mark it handled once you have dealt with it.
incidents.noticed_hint: The hub carried on by itself (deferred, retried, or the agent simply kept working). Kept as history and closed automatically once the run finishes.
incidents.resolve_hint: Clearing an entry only silences it here and on Telegram — it changes nothing about the run. If the problem occurs again, the entry reopens and Telegram notifies again.
repos.name: Name
repos.extras_invalid: Worktree extras: expected a list of {"path": "…", "mode": "copy"|"link"}.
repos.extras_json: Worktree extras are not valid JSON: {err}
repos.extras_find_hint: a model looks at the repository and suggests what a worktree should carry — the current list is REPLACED
repos.extras_dialog_hint: The hub first checks that the path exists and is a git repository; only then does a model look at the repository and suggest extras.
repos.extras_warn: This completely replaces the current worktree extras. A model generates the whole list from scratch — existing entries are not kept.
repos.extras_working: Looking at the repository and asking the model …
repos.extras_llm_off: Worktree-extras LLM is switched off or OPENROUTER_API_KEY is missing (Settings → Worktree extras).
repos.extras_parse: The model answered something that is not JSON.
repos.prompt_label: Repo prompt (added to every run of this repo — agents and single runs alike)
repos.merge_flows_none: No flow runs after a merge of this repo.
sessions.title: tmux sessions
sessions.intro: Every run works in its own tmux session, and it deliberately outlives the agent so the screen stays readable. Until it is closed, the agent's process keeps its memory — this is where you end them, oldest first.
sessions.show_running: Also show sessions with a running agent
sessions.auto_hint: Finished sessions close by themselves after {hours} h.
sessions.hidden_note: Sessions with a running agent right now: {n}. They stay hidden by default so none is ended by a misclick.
sessions.unknown_hint: no run of this hub — only ended by hand
sessions.aborted_note: The tmux session was ended before the run reported a result. The run therefore counts as aborted.
settings.global_hint: These settings apply globally to the whole hub — not to the repo selected above. Repo-specific are only the entries under Repos (path, base branch, worktree extras, repo prompt) and the agents themselves.
settings.coding_agents_hint: add, edit or remove coding agents and their providers
settings.gates_hint: A gate defers a start when the account behind that provider is nearly exhausted. Each gate is optional: switch it off and starts pass regardless of the window. Deferred runs can be started anyway from their detail page.
settings.gate_claude_7d_hint: The general week; a run on a per-model week is measured against its own threshold.
settings.gate_claude_fable_hint: Own threshold for the Fable week. Empty = the 7-day threshold applies.
settings.gate_deepseek_min_hint: A CNY-only DeepSeek account reports no USD — the gate stays open there.
settings.session_keep_hint: 0 = close it right away. Counts from whichever comes first: the run's end or the exit of its process. Sessions are listed and ended by hand under Sessions.
settings.flow_runs_keep_hint: Finished flow runs (done/stopped) older than this are deleted; failed ones are kept 4× as long so a problem stays visible. 0 = keep forever.
settings.prompt_suffix: Platform prompt suffix — added to the built-in platform rules for every run (placeholders {run_id} {workdir} {report_file} {branch_rule} {expected_minutes}). The rules themselves, and the finishing command, always stay; for rules that only concern one repository use the repo prompt.
settings.llm_legend: Check LLM for log hits (optional, via OpenRouter)
settings.llm_hint: The scanner finds lines that look like a rate limit or provider error. With the check LLM on, it receives the last terminal lines and decides in a structured way whether the agent is really blocked (immediately red) or whether it was a menu line/retry (no incident). Off: hits turn yellow and become red after repetition or 5 min of silence. Applies to all agents. At most one request per run and 10 minutes.
settings.llm_missing_key: OPENROUTER_API_KEY is missing in ~/.config/cc-hub/env — without a key this stays off.
settings.llm_mru_hint: list: the 10 most recently saved models
settings.title_hint: A single run whose title field stayed empty gets one from the prompt. A very cheap model is enough for this — a title costs a fraction of a cent. Off, without a key or on any error the run keeps the first line of its prompt as its title; nothing ever fails over a title.
settings.title_model_hint: empty = {model}; the list holds the default and the models saved most recently
settings.extras_hint: The repo form's "Find worktree extras" asks a model to look at the repository and suggest what a worktree should carry beyond what git tracks (a .env, a linked node_modules). Off, without a key or on any error the button simply reports the reason — nothing else depends on it.
settings.extras_model_hint: empty = {model}; the list holds the default and the models saved most recently
settings.telegram_fail: Telegram test message failed — are token and chat ID set? See the assistant.
ca.title: Coding agents
ca.intro: Which coding agent CLIs may this hub drive, and which model providers may each of them use? Forms only offer what is configured and enabled here.
ca.all_configured: All available coding agents are already configured.
ca.detect_note: Detection: for each known coding agent the hub checks whether its CLI is installed on this machine (command -v). New coding agents are added as plugins — see docs/plugins.md.
ca.providers_hint: Only selected providers appear in the forms — and of those only the ones with credentials (or key-free access).
ca.no_providers: subscription-based — the models come from the account, there is no provider selection
ca.delete_confirm: Really remove the coding agent "{label}"? Existing agents and runs keep their data.
settings.favorites_hint: save up to three setups (coding agent, provider, model, effort, extra skills, flows) and start a run from them anywhere
fav.title: Favorites
fav.intro: A favorite is the setup of a run under a name: coding agent, provider, model, reasoning effort, extra skills and attached flows. The task, the branch rule and the start time are not part of it — those are asked for at the Quick Run, together with the favorite.
fav.full: All {max} slots are in use — edit or remove one of them.
fav.name: Name
fav.err_full: There is room for {max} favorites — remove one first.
fav.err_name_taken: There is already a favorite called "{name}".
qr.title: Quick Run
qr.hint: Start a run from a favorite — from any page, without leaving it.
qr.favorite_info: the setup this favorite starts with
qr.no_repo: There is no repo yet — a run needs one.
qr.no_favorite: There is no favorite yet. A Quick Run starts from one, so create one first.
qr.err_favorite: This favorite does not exist (any more).
form.goal_too_long: The goal is {len} characters long — at most {max} are allowed.
form.branch_missing: Branch pattern is missing (expectation is not "none").
run.branch_in_use: Branch "{branch}" is already checked out in {worktree} — git grants a branch to only one worktree. Pick a branch that is free, or the expectation "new branch" / "none".
form.subscription_no_provider: {harness} runs on its subscription — there is no provider selection, only the model.
form.provider_unavailable: Provider "{provider}" is not available for {harness} here (missing key or not enabled?). Possible: {list}
form.effort_invalid: Reasoning effort "{effort}" is not possible for {target} — possible: {list}
effort.claude_cli: levels according to claude --help; applies to all subscription models
effort.cursor_in_id: cursor encodes the reasoning effort into the model ID (e.g. …-low, …-high, …-xhigh, …-max) — the level is already part of the model choice
effort.registry_only: levels according to the model catalog — opencode only accepts these
effort.none_in_catalog: the catalog lists no effort levels for this model
effort.intersection: levels known to BOTH hermes and the model
effort.no_common: hermes and the model have no common level
effort.model_unknown: no effort levels known for this model
sched.kind_weekly: on weekdays at a fixed time
sched.once_hint: Runs exactly once and resets itself to "manual" afterwards. If the hub was off at the date, the start is caught up.
sched.cron_hint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday.
sched.err_days: Please select at least one weekday.
sched.err_time: Time is missing or invalid (format HH:MM).
sched.err_anchor: A multi-week interval needs an anchor week.
sched.err_cron: "{expr}" is not a 5-field cron (minute hour day month weekday), e.g. "0 6 * * 1-5".
model.model_ph: Type a slug or pick from the list
or.hint: Without the checkbox OpenRouter decides itself. Only possible for opencode — hermes has no per-run argument for this.
tg.title: Telegram setup
tg.step1_hint: In Telegram open @BotFather → /newbot (or /mybots → existing bot) → copy the token (form 123456789:AA…).
tg.step2_hint: Send your bot a message in Telegram (e.g. /start) and then click:
tg.step3_hint: Then you are done — notifications go out for: done / failed / help call / anomaly / start deferred / quota ≥ 80 %. Every message has an "Open detail page" button.
tg.no_chats: No messages found. Write to the bot first (/start), then click again.
tg.token_invalid: This does not look like a BotFather token.
js.providers_with_creds: only providers that are enabled for this coding agent and have credentials here
js.no_creds: no providers available for this coding agent — type the model freely
js.provider_list_unreachable: provider list unreachable — type the model freely
js.list_unreachable: List unreachable ({err}) — type the model slug directly.
js.stale: (list currently unreachable, showing the last state)
js.from_catalog: from the vendor catalog: not everything in it is usable here without a key
js.cursor_note: The reasoning effort is part of the ID (…-low/-medium/-high/-xhigh/-max); IDs ending in "-fast" are cursor's fast mode — the default is the variant without.
js.type_filter: Typing filters; a custom slug is always allowed.
js.auto_tag: Auto — Cursor picks the model (draws on its own pool of the included usage)
js.no_endpoints: — no data, type the slug below —
js.sessions_hidden: Sessions with a running agent, hidden: {n}
js.sessions_kill_confirm: {n} of these sessions still have a running agent — it is killed along with the session. Continue?
js.no_session: No tmux session anymore — the history is in the log below.
flows.intro: Flows react to finished runs (or a schedule) with no-code building blocks: message running agents, extract structured data from a report, start follow-up agents, notify via Telegram.
flows.name: Name
flows.delete_confirm: Delete this flow? Its past flow runs stay in the history.
flows.trigger.run_merged.desc: Starts once per merge into the base branch, with the run whose work landed — also when a conflict run was needed to make it mergeable.
flows.trigger.manual_hint: Only via "run now" — optionally with a finished run as the simulated trigger.
flows.trigger.unattached: not attached to any agent yet
flows.when.not_done: when it failed or was aborted
flows.attach.hint: When the run has finished, every ticked flow starts — all of them in parallel. The condition here does not replace the "Switch on outcome" block inside a flow; it decides whether the flow starts at all.
flows.attach.none: No flow reacts to finished runs yet.
flows.attach.editor_none: This flow hangs on no agent — it will not start on its own.
flows.attach.editor_hint: Which agents start this flow when their run ends. The very same list is edited in the agent form; a single run picks its flows in the single-run form.
flows.attach.run_none: No flow was attached to this run.
flows.runs.title: Flow runs
flows.editor.name_taken: A flow with this name already exists.
flows.editor.cron_invalid: The cron expression is not valid (5 fields).
flows.editor.variables_hint: Use {{…}} in any text field. Click to copy. Objects render as JSON; missing values as empty text. {{x | default: text}} sets a fallback.
flows.editor.sim_none: run now without a trigger run
flows.editor.run_unsaved: There are unsaved changes — run the saved version anyway?
flows.step.send_message.desc: Types a message into the tmux session of running runs (e.g. "main has moved, please pull").
flows.step.start_agent.desc: Starts a configured agent, optionally with extra prompt text. With "wait" the flow pauses until that run ends and stores its result.
flows.step.start_single_run.desc: Starts an ad-hoc run with its own prompt (as in the single-run form). With "wait" the flow pauses until it ends.
flows.step.kill_run.desc: Kills the tmux session of the selected running runs and marks them aborted.
flows.step.extract.desc: An LLM (OpenRouter, check-LLM settings) reads the report and/or terminal log of a run and fills the fields you define.
flows.step.set_var.desc: Stores a value under vars.<name>. A single {{path}} keeps its type, anything else becomes text.
flows.step.http_request.desc: Calls a webhook/API. The response (status, body, json) is stored in the output variable.
flows.step.shell_command.desc: Runs a command on the hub machine. A non-zero exit code is a result the flow can branch on, not a failure of the step.
flows.step.condition.desc: Compares two values and continues in the true or false branch.
flows.step.switch_outcome.desc: Branches on done / failed / aborted (by default the trigger run's outcome).
flows.step.for_each.desc: Repeats the steps inside it once per element of a list — e.g. the open points from an extraction.
flows.step.delay.desc: Pauses the flow for the given minutes (survives a hub restart).
flows.step.telegram.desc: Sends a message over the configured Telegram bot, optionally with an attachment (e.g. the report).
flows.step.note.desc: Writes a line into the flow run log — handy for checking variables.
flows.field.wait: wait until the run ends (result → output variable)
flows.field.sourceRun.hint: Run ID or template; default: the trigger run.
flows.field.command.hint: Runs as the hub's user on the hub machine. Templates like {{trigger.merge.sha}} are allowed.
flows.field.cwd.hint: Where the command runs; empty = the hub user's home directory.
flows.field.detach.hint: Start the command in the background and continue at once. Tick this for a command that restarts cc-hub itself and prefix it with "sleep 3;" — otherwise the flow run dies with the hub and stays "running" forever.
flows.field.list.hint: Template yielding a list ({{vars.extracted.open_points}}); plain text is split line by line.
flows.field.itemVar.hint: The current element is vars.<name>, its position vars.<name>_index.
flows.editor.var_conditional: set inside a branch or loop — may be missing here
flows.editor.value_none: This operator compares nothing — no value needed.
flows.trigger.cron_no_run: A schedule has no trigger run: {{trigger.run.…}} stays empty, and steps that need a run outcome are only valid after a start step with "wait".
flows.warn.bool_value: {path} is a yes/no value — only "true" or "false" can ever match
flows.warn.number_value: {path} is a number — this value is not one
flows.warn.op_type: This operator cannot answer anything about {path} ({type})
flows.warn.needs_run_maybe: needs a finished run — a manual flow only has one when "run now" is given one
flows.placement.needs_run.rule: Needs a finished run: either from the trigger ("run finished") or from an earlier "Start agent" / "Start single run" with "wait".
flows.placement.needs_run.why: "{step}" cannot sit here: no finished run is available at this point, so the step could only ever take its fallback branch. Put it after a start step with "wait", or give the flow a "run finished" trigger.
flows.placement.needs_run_maybe.why: "{step}" only has a run when "run now" is given one — otherwise it falls through to its fallback.
flows.placement.after_stop.why: Nothing can follow "Stop" — the flow run has already ended there.
flows.placement.needs_run_target.rule: Only the target "the trigger run" needs a finished run. Every other target — an agent, a repo, all running runs, a run ID — reaches runs that have nothing to do with this flow and works in any flow.
flows.placement.needs_run_target.why: "{step}" is aimed at the trigger run, but there is none here. Pick another target — an agent, a repo or all running runs also reach agents outside this flow — or give the flow a "run finished" trigger.
flows.placement.needs_run_target_maybe.w: "{step}" is aimed at the trigger run, which a manual flow only has when "run now" is given one. Any other target works regardless.
flows.warn.needs_run_target_maybe: aimed at the trigger run — a manual flow only has one when "run now" is given one
side.title: Status
settings.abo_price_hint: The monthly price, used to account a run against the subscription.
settings.cursor_included_hint: Included monthly usage — a fallback only: normally Cursor reports it itself.
repos.merge_mode_hint: off: the run ends when the agent reports done; nothing is merged (today's behaviour). hub: cc-hub checks the worktree, merges the run's branch into the base branch itself and escalates only when the agent does not deliver.
repos.merge_check_hint: Shell command run on the merged result before it is pushed, e.g. `node test/unit.mjs`. Empty = none. A red check is treated like a conflict: the agent gets the output and must fix it.
repos.finish_timeout_hint: How long cc-hub waits for the agent to commit or resolve after it reported done. Then it escalates: a conflict run for conflicts, you for uncommitted changes.
repos.merge_max_attempts_hint: How many conflict runs may try before cc-hub asks you.
repos.conflict_parallel_hint: How many conflict runs may work at the same time in this repo. Keep 1 for small repos where tasks touch the same files — parallel resolvers then invalidate each other and only the first one's work survives. Raise it for large repos where conflicts rarely touch the same files.
repos.notify_running: Tell the running agents about a merge
repos.notify_running_hint: After a merge, tell the other running agents of this repo that the base branch moved — urgently if the merge touched files they are working on.
repos.max_parallel_hint: Upper bound of running runs in this repo for scheduled starts; 0 = unlimited. Manual starts are never blocked.
repos.err_number: {field}: a whole number of at least {min} is expected.
merge.settings_intro: When a finished run's branch no longer merges into the base branch and its agent is gone, cc-hub starts a conflict run: an ordinary single run whose whole task is to make that branch mergeable again. This is the setup it starts with — coding agent, provider, model, effort and extra skills.
merge.no_resolver_hint: Without a resolver, a conflicting branch is escalated to you directly.
merge.resolver_prompt: Additional instructions for the conflict resolver
merge.resolver_prompt_hint: Appended to every conflict run's task. Repo rules belong in the repo prompt, not here.
merge.discard_confirm: Discard the uncommitted changes in this worktree? This cannot be undone.
merge.unmerged_both: not merged: commits and uncommitted changes
merge.err_still_dirty: The worktree still has uncommitted changes — nothing was merged.
merge.err_no_resolver: The branch conflicts with the base branch, and no conflict resolver is configured (Settings → Merge).
branch.none.explain_off: The worktree is detached. Nothing is kept unless the agent pushes it somewhere itself — throwaway work.
branch.none.explain_hub: The worktree is detached; cc-hub merges the commits into {base} when the run is done. If it needs a name (backup, conflict run) it uses `run/<id>`.
branch.new.explain_off: A new branch from the pattern. Whether it ever reaches {base} is up to the agent — or to you.
branch.new.explain_hub: A new branch from the pattern; cc-hub merges it into {base} when the run is done. Pick this for a readable name on origin.
branch.fixed.explain_off: Continue on an existing branch across several runs.
branch.fixed.explain_hub: Continue on an existing branch; cc-hub merges it into {base} after every run — tick “keep on branch” below to leave the work there instead.
branch.keep: Keep the work on its branch — do not merge into {base}
branch.keep.hint: Only while the repo integrates; ignored otherwise.
form.keep_needs_branch: Keeping the work on a branch needs a branch — choose “new” or “existing”.
